summary:
Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha is a British Overseas Territory. United Kingdom legislation reaches it only where extended by order, so the territory's own ordinances and institutions determine what a visitor encounters. No transgender-specific criminal, documentation, screening, facilities, custody, care or violence provision is documented in territory law.

Consensual same-sex activity has been lawful since 2001, and the age of consent is equalised at 16 across Saint Helena, Ascension Island and Tristan da Cunha. No penalty provision specific to transgender people is documented anywhere in the territory's instruments.

The St Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha Constitution Order 2009 has been in force since 2009 and bans discrimination on grounds including sex and sexual orientation. It defines "discriminatory" as affording different treatment to different persons on any ground such as sex, sexual orientation, race, colour, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, association with a national minority, property, age, disability, birth or other status. The ban is written around sexual orientation, and no source documents it being applied to gender reassignment.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission in Saint Helena monitors human rights laws, promotes understanding of the importance of equality and works towards the elimination of unlawful discrimination. Under the Commission for Equality and Human Rights Ordinance 2015 it may conduct inquiries and investigations into persons suspected of having committed an unlawful act, including unlawful discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or "gender reassignment". That ordinance defines "gender reassignment" as an intended, current or past process, or part of such a process, for the purpose of reassigning a person's sex by changing physiological or other attributes of sex, or the state of mind whereby a person psychologically identifies with a gender inconsistent with or not culturally associated with their assigned sex at birth. This is the only transgender-specific wording located in territory law, and it sits in the commission's enabling ordinance rather than in a criminal, documentation or entry instrument.

Marriage is available to same-sex couples on all three islands. The Marriage (Ascension) Ordinance 2016 commenced on 1 January 2017, the Marriages (Tristan da Cunha) Ordinance 2017 took effect on 4 August 2017, and the Marriage Ordinance 2017 took effect on Saint Helena on 20 December 2017. The Tristan da Cunha ordinance defines marriage as the union of two persons regardless of sex and extends eligibility, formalities, rights and recognition to same-sex couples on equal terms with opposite-sex couples. The first same-sex marriage recorded in Saint Helena took place on 31 December 2018. A trans visitor in what would be locally classed as a same-sex relationship can therefore marry on any of the three islands.
tangentialFactors:
The territory is classed as an Overseas Country or Territory of the European Union, and a source accessed on 23 June 2013 states that the EU Charter applies to it. That claim is dated and its current standing is not sourced here.

Protections are territory-wide rather than confined to one island: the discrimination ban has operated across all three constituent islands since 2009, the age of consent is equalised at 16 throughout, and marriage was extended to same-sex couples on each island within a single year, 2017.

The legislative record shows no contested passage. The Ascension Island Council approved the marriage ordinance on 31 May 2016 by five votes to nil, and the ordinance was signed and gazetted on 20 June 2016 before commencing on 1 January 2017.
localsOnly:
Adoption law does not turn on sexual orientation. Under the Saint Helena Welfare of Children Ordinance 2010, which covers Saint Helena and Tristan da Cunha, and the Ascension Island Child Welfare Ordinance 2011, single and married people may adopt regardless of sexual orientation. A 2006 United Kingdom Government report recorded that no adoptions had taken place in Saint Helena or Ascension Island for many years, and no more recent figure is sourced.

The Commission for Equality and Human Rights Ordinance 2015 defines sexual orientation as a person's sexual orientation towards persons of the same sex, persons of the opposite sex, or persons of either sex. The commission's mandate covers monitoring human rights laws, promoting understanding of the importance of equality, working towards elimination of unlawful discrimination, and conducting inquiries and investigations into suspected unlawful acts including discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender reassignment.

The Ascension marriage ordinance was approved by the Ascension Island Council on 31 May 2016 by five votes to nil, signed and gazetted on 20 June 2016, and commenced on 1 January 2017. The equivalent instruments for Tristan da Cunha and Saint Helena commenced on 4 August 2017 and 20 December 2017 respectively.
